subject: general
question: A flame is made up of three parts: the innermost part, the middle part and the outermost part. Why is the innermost part black?

options.text: Because of complete combustion of fuel
Because of the incomplete combustion of fuel
Because of the presence of un-burnt carbon particles
Because of the presence of oxygen

solution:
The correct answer is __**Because of the presence of un-burnt carbon particles**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The innermost part of a flame is black due to the **presence of un-burnt carbon particles**.
 
• In this region, the fuel is not completely combusted, leading to the presence of these particles.
 
• This part of the flame is also known as the dark zone or the non-luminous zone.
 
• The incomplete combustion in this zone occurs due to a lack of sufficient oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Complete combustion occurs in the outermost part of the flame where there is an ample supply of oxygen.
 
• The middle part of the flame is moderately hot and partially luminous, due to partial combustion.
 
• Understanding the different zones of a flame is crucial in various scientific applications, including analysis of combustion efficiency and safety measures in industrial processes.
